<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
library(ggplot2)

cell_press_spec &lt;- spec_get(&quot;cell_press&quot;)
report_spec &lt;- spec_get(list(
  name = &quot;Clinical research report&quot;,
  columns = list(half = 80, full = 160),
  formats = &quot;png&quot;,
  dpi_min = 300
))

columns_plot &lt;- ggplot(
  mpg,
  aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv, shape = drv)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = &quot;Fuel economy by engine size&quot;,
    x = &quot;Engine displacement (litres)&quot;,
    y = &quot;Highway fuel economy&quot;,
    colour = &quot;Drive layout&quot;,
    shape = &quot;Drive layout&quot;
  ) +
  fig_apply_spec(cell_press_spec, base_size = 10)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>The specification to inspect: a registry id, a figspec_spec, or a named list of requirements.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a registry id, an existing specification or a named list. The example lists widths from both Cell Press and a project specification, then uses Cell Press's one-and-a-half-column choice to export and check a real figure.</p><pre><code class="language-r">publisher_columns &lt;- fig_columns(
  &quot;cell_press&quot;
)

project_columns &lt;- fig_columns(
  report_spec
)

selected_column &lt;- names(
  publisher_columns
)[2]

output_file &lt;- file.path(
  tempdir(),
  &quot;cell-press-onehalf-width.tiff&quot;
)

saved_file &lt;- fig_save(
  output_file,
  columns_plot,
  spec = cell_press_spec,
  column = selected_column,
  height = 80,
  dpi = 300,
  check = FALSE
)

saved_check &lt;- fig_check(
  saved_file,
  spec = cell_press_spec,
  column = selected_column,
  dpi = 300
)

publisher_columns
project_columns
saved_check[
  saved_check$check == &quot;Width&quot;,
  c(&quot;requirement&quot;, &quot;actual&quot;, &quot;status&quot;)
]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Cell Press lists single, onehalf and double widths of 85, 114 and 174 mm. The project lists half and full widths of 80 and 160 mm. The TIFF exported with the onehalf choice passes its 114 mm saved-width check.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `spec_register()`

Register a publication specification for this session

Add a publication specification that is not bundled with figspec. The new entry is available throughout the current R session and is marked as user-supplied whenever the registry is listed.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
library(ggplot2)

registered_spec &lt;- spec_register(
  id = &quot;research_methods_review&quot;,
  name = &quot;Research Methods Review&quot;,
  source_url = &quot;internal:author-guidelines-v2&quot;,
  verified_on = Sys.Date(),
  requirements = list(
    columns = list(single = 85, full = 170),
    height_max_mm = 220,
    dpi_min = 300,
    formats = c(&quot;png&quot;, &quot;pdf&quot;),
    font_min_pt = 9,
    font_max_pt = 12,
    colour_mode = &quot;RGB&quot;,
    max_file_mb = 20
  ),
  not_stated = c(
    &quot;font_families&quot;, &quot;min_line_pt&quot;, &quot;max_line_pt&quot;,
    &quot;avoid_colour_pairs&quot;, &quot;print_greyscale&quot;
  ),
  house_style = list(
    palette = c(&quot;#1B4965&quot;, &quot;#CA6702&quot;, &quot;#5C677D&quot;)
  ),
  publisher = &quot;Example Research Society&quot;,
  disciplines = c(&quot;health&quot;, &quot;statistics&quot;),
  publication_stage = &quot;all&quot;,
  notes = &quot;Example requirements for demonstrating a user entry.&quot;
)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>id</code></td><td>A short, unique identifier beginning with a lower-case letter and containing only lower-case letters, numbers and underscores. This is the value supplied to functions such as fig_save(spec = &quot;my_journal&quot;).<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Choose a short identifier that begins with a lower-case letter and uses only lower-case letters, numbers and underscores. This is the name used in later figspec calls. An id already used by a bundled profile is rejected so that a local entry cannot silently hide it.</p><pre><code class="language-r">registered_spec$id

same_entry &lt;- spec_get(
  &quot;research_methods_review&quot;
)

identical(
  same_entry,
  registered_spec
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The entry can be retrieved with research_methods_review, and the retrieved specification is identical to the one returned when it was registered.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>name</code></td><td>The publication name shown in reports and registry listings.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Give the publication its full readable name. figspec uses this text in check reports and messages, while id remains the shorter name used in code.</p><pre><code class="language-r">c(
  id = registered_spec$id,
  name = registered_spec$name
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Reports identify the specification as Research Methods Review while R code can continue to use its shorter id.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>source_url</code></td><td>Where the requirements came from: an HTTP(S) page, a file: URI or an internal: identifier.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Record where the requirements came from. Use the public HTTP or HTTPS guidance page when available; use a file: URI or an internal: label for a private handbook or organisational decision.</p><pre><code class="language-r">registered_spec$source_url</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The example records internal:author-guidelines-v2, making clear that this source is maintained by the user rather than bundled by figspec.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>verified_on</code></td><td>Date the source was last checked, as &quot;YYYY-MM-DD&quot; or a Date. Future and invalid dates are rejected.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Record when the source was last checked. Supply a Date or a real date in YYYY-MM-DD form. figspec rejects invalid dates and dates in the future.</p><pre><code class="language-r">registered_spec$verified_on</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The entry stores today's date in YYYY-MM-DD form as its most recent source check.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>requirements</code></td><td>A named list containing only requirements stated by the source, such as columns, dpi_min, formats, font_min_pt or min_line_pt. Values are validated before the entry is registered.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Include only rules stated by the source. Common fields cover figure widths, maximum height, resolution, formats, type size, line weight, colour mode and file size. The example applies these requirements to all 234 mpg observations, exports a real PNG and checks the saved file.</p><pre><code class="language-r">registered_plot &lt;- ggplot(
  mpg,
  aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv, shape = drv)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = &quot;Fuel economy by engine size&quot;,
    x = &quot;Engine displacement (litres)&quot;,
    y = &quot;Highway fuel economy&quot;,
    colour = &quot;Drive layout&quot;,
    shape = &quot;Drive layout&quot;
  ) +
  fig_apply_spec(
    &quot;research_methods_review&quot;,
    base_size = 10
  )

output_file &lt;- file.path(
  tempdir(),
  &quot;registered-publication-figure.png&quot;
)

saved_file &lt;- fig_save(
  output_file,
  registered_plot,
  spec = &quot;research_methods_review&quot;,
  column = &quot;single&quot;,
  height = 90,
  dpi = 300
)

saved_report &lt;- attr(
  saved_file,
  &quot;figspec_report&quot;
)

registered_plot
saved_report[
  saved_report$check %in% c(
    &quot;Width&quot;, &quot;Resolution&quot;, &quot;File format&quot;, &quot;Type size&quot;
  ),
  c(&quot;check&quot;, &quot;requirement&quot;, &quot;actual&quot;, &quot;status&quot;)
]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The plot is built with the registered type and line rules, saved at the 85 mm single width and 300 dpi, and passes the saved-file checks for width, resolution, PNG format and type size.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>house_style</code></td><td>Optional named visual preferences, such as list(palette = c(&quot;#1B4965&quot;, &quot;#CA6702&quot;)). Requirements do not belong here and are rejected if included.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Store optional visual preferences separately from requirements. A palette can identify the publication without being treated as a rule that determines compliance. Invalid colours and requirement fields are rejected here.</p><pre><code class="language-r">publication_colours &lt;- spec_style_palette(
  &quot;research_methods_review&quot;
)

house_style_plot &lt;- ggplot(
  mpg,
  aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv, shape = drv)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = publication_colours
  ) +
  labs(
    title = &quot;The publication's optional palette&quot;,
    x = &quot;Engine displacement (litres)&quot;,
    y = &quot;Highway fuel economy&quot;,
    colour = &quot;Drive layout&quot;,
    shape = &quot;Drive layout&quot;
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

publication_colours
house_style_plot</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The three recorded colours are applied to the three drive layouts. The palette remains a design choice and is not counted as a publication requirement by fig_check().</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>...</code></td><td>Optional registry information such as publisher, disciplines, publication_stage, notes, tables, media or graphical_abstract.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Add useful context such as the publisher, disciplines, publication stage, notes, table rules or media rules. These fields make the entry easier to find and interpret without changing the figure requirements.</p><pre><code class="language-r">profile_row &lt;- spec_list()
profile_row &lt;- profile_row[
  profile_row$id == &quot;research_methods_review&quot;,
  c(
    &quot;id&quot;, &quot;name&quot;, &quot;publisher&quot;, &quot;disciplines&quot;,
    &quot;publication_stage&quot;, &quot;origin&quot;
  )
]

profile_row</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The registry listing shows the publication name, publisher, health and statistics disciplines, all-stage scope and user origin recorded by the additional fields.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `spec_save()`

Save a specification for reuse

Save a publication, project or organisational specification in a YAML file that figspec can load in later R sessions. figspec validates the complete file before replacing anything, so a failed update leaves the previous registry intact.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
reusable_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Research unit report&quot;,
  columns = list(full = 160),
  dpi_min = 300,
  formats = c(&quot;png&quot;, &quot;pdf&quot;),
  font_min_pt = 9,
  tables = list(
    formats = c(&quot;html&quot;, &quot;docx&quot;),
    font_min_pt = 9,
    header_bold = TRUE,
    vertical_rules = FALSE
  )
)

spec_output_dir &lt;- tempfile(&quot;figspec-spec-save-&quot;)
dir.create(spec_output_dir)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>A registry id, a figspec_spec, or a named list containing at least a non-empty name and any figure, table, media or graphical-abstract requirements to save.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a registry id, a specification returned by spec_get() or a named list of your own requirements. Figure and table requirements are stored together and retain their separate structure.</p><pre><code class="language-r">specification_file &lt;- file.path(
  spec_output_dir,
  &quot;saved-list.yml&quot;
)
spec_save(
  reusable_spec,
  specification_file,
  id = &quot;research_unit_report&quot;
)
saved_entry &lt;- yaml::read_yaml(
  specification_file,
  eval.expr = FALSE
)$specifications[[1]]

c(
  name = saved_entry$name,
  figure_width_mm = saved_entry$requirements$columns$full,
  table_font_pt = saved_entry$tables$font_min_pt
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The saved entry retains the report name, its 160 mm figure width and its 9 pt table-text requirement in one validated file.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>path</code></td><td>Destination .yaml or .yml file. If it already contains a valid figspec registry, a new id is appended without removing the other entries.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Choose a .yaml or .yml file in an existing directory. Keep it with the project or in a shared version-controlled folder, then pass the same path to spec_load() when an R session starts.</p><pre><code class="language-r">project_registry &lt;- file.path(
  spec_output_dir,
  &quot;project-specifications.yml&quot;
)
saved_path &lt;- spec_save(
  reusable_spec,
  project_registry,
  id = &quot;project_report&quot;
)

c(
  path = saved_path,
  exists = file.exists(saved_path),
  valid = suppressMessages(
    registry_validate_file(saved_path)
  )
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> figspec creates project-specifications.yml, validates it and returns the supplied path invisibly.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>id</code></td><td>A short identifier beginning with a lower-case letter and containing only lower-case letters, numbers and underscores. It may be omitted when spec already contains an id.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Give the specification a short stable identifier. This is the name used in later calls after spec_load(); lower-case letters, numbers and underscores are accepted.</p><pre><code class="language-r">id_file &lt;- file.path(spec_output_dir, &quot;id-example.yml&quot;)
spec_save(
  reusable_spec,
  id_file,
  id = &quot;quarterly_report&quot;
)
spec_load(id_file)

loaded_spec &lt;- spec_get(&quot;quarterly_report&quot;)
c(id = loaded_spec$id, name = loaded_spec$name)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The YAML entry is loaded under quarterly_report while reports display the readable name Research unit report.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>source_url</code></td><td>Where the requirements came from: an HTTP(S) page, a file: URI or an internal: identifier. When omitted, an existing value in spec is kept; otherwise internal:&lt;id&gt; is recorded.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Record where the requirements came from. Use a public HTTP or HTTPS page when one exists, a file: address for a controlled local document, or an internal: label for an organisational decision. If this argument and the specification both omit a source, figspec records internal:id.</p><pre><code class="language-r">source_file &lt;- file.path(spec_output_dir, &quot;source-example.yml&quot;)
spec_save(
  reusable_spec,
  source_file,
  id = &quot;methods_handbook&quot;,
  source_url = &quot;internal:methods-handbook-v3&quot;
)
yaml::read_yaml(
  source_file,
  eval.expr = FALSE
)$specifications[[1]]$source_url</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The reusable entry records internal:methods-handbook-v3 instead of implying that its requirements came from a publisher.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>verified_on</code></td><td>Date the source or internal requirements were last checked, as &quot;YYYY-MM-DD&quot; or a Date. When omitted, an existing value in spec is kept; otherwise today's date is recorded.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Record when the source or internal requirements were last checked. Use a Date or a real date in YYYY-MM-DD form. If it is omitted everywhere, figspec records the day the specification is saved.</p><pre><code class="language-r">dated_file &lt;- file.path(spec_output_dir, &quot;dated-example.yml&quot;)
review_date &lt;- Sys.Date() - 30
spec_save(
  reusable_spec,
  dated_file,
  id = &quot;reviewed_report&quot;,
  verified_on = review_date
)
yaml::read_yaml(
  dated_file,
  eval.expr = FALSE
)$specifications[[1]]$verified_on</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The YAML file retains the supplied review date in YYYY-MM-DD form so users can see when the requirements were last checked.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>overwrite</code></td><td>Whether an entry with the same id may be replaced. Other entries in the file are always preserved.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Leave overwrite as FALSE to prevent an existing id from being replaced accidentally. Set it to TRUE only when deliberately updating that specification; every other entry in the file is preserved.</p><pre><code class="language-r">update_file &lt;- file.path(spec_output_dir, &quot;updates.yml&quot;)
spec_save(
  reusable_spec,
  update_file,
  id = &quot;annual_report&quot;
)
spec_save(
  list(name = &quot;Poster format&quot;, columns = list(full = 900)),
  update_file,
  id = &quot;conference_poster&quot;
)
spec_save(
  c(reusable_spec, list(notes = &quot;Reviewed for the new report cycle&quot;)),
  update_file,
  id = &quot;annual_report&quot;,
  overwrite = TRUE
)

updated_ids &lt;- vapply(
  yaml::read_yaml(
    update_file,
    eval.expr = FALSE
  )$specifications,
  function(entry) entry$id,
  character(1)
)
updated_ids</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> annual_report is deliberately replaced and conference_poster remains in the same file; without overwrite = TRUE, figspec refuses the duplicate id.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `spec_load()`

Load specifications from a YAML registry

Load one or more reusable specifications from a YAML file maintained by a publication, project or organisation. Loaded entries remain separate from figspec's bundled profiles and last for the current R session.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
library(ggplot2)

registry_file &lt;- file.path(
  tempdir(),
  &quot;research-unit-specifications.yml&quot;
)

yaml::write_yaml(
  list(
    specifications = list(
      list(
        id = &quot;research_unit_report&quot;,
        name = &quot;Research Unit Report&quot;,
        publisher = &quot;Example Research Unit&quot;,
        disciplines = c(&quot;health&quot;, &quot;economics&quot;),
        source_url = &quot;internal:report-guide-v4&quot;,
        verified_on = as.character(Sys.Date()),
        requirements = list(
          columns = list(half = 80, full = 160),
          height_max_mm = 120,
          dpi_min = 300,
          formats = c(&quot;png&quot;, &quot;pdf&quot;),
          font_min_pt = 9,
          font_max_pt = 12,
          colour_mode = &quot;RGB&quot;,
          max_file_mb = 20
        ),
        not_stated = c(
          &quot;font_families&quot;, &quot;min_line_pt&quot;, &quot;max_line_pt&quot;,
          &quot;avoid_colour_pairs&quot;, &quot;print_greyscale&quot;
        ),
        house_style = list(
          palette = c(&quot;#1B4965&quot;, &quot;#CA6702&quot;, &quot;#5C677D&quot;)
        )
      )
    )
  ),
  registry_file
)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>path</code></td><td>Path to a non-empty YAML registry file. The file may contain a top-level specifications: list written by spec_save(), the legacy journals: list used by figspec's bundled registry, or be the list of entries itself.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply the path to a YAML registry. The entire file is validated before anything is added. The example loads one specification, applies it to all 574 observations in ggplot2's economics data, exports a real PNG and verifies the result.</p><pre><code class="language-r">loaded_ids &lt;- spec_load(
  registry_file
)

loaded_spec &lt;- spec_get(
  &quot;research_unit_report&quot;
)

loaded_plot &lt;- ggplot(
  economics,
  aes(date, unemploy)
) +
  geom_line(
    colour = &quot;#1B4965&quot;,
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  labs(
    title = &quot;Unemployment over time&quot;,
    subtitle = &quot;A 574-month example using a loaded specification&quot;,
    x = NULL,
    y = &quot;People unemployed (thousands)&quot;,
    caption = &quot;Source: ggplot2::economics&quot;
  ) +
  fig_apply_spec(
    loaded_spec,
    colour = FALSE,
    shapes = FALSE,
    base_size = 10
  )

output_file &lt;- file.path(
  tempdir(),
  &quot;research-unit-report-figure.png&quot;
)

saved_file &lt;- fig_save(
  output_file,
  loaded_plot,
  spec = loaded_spec,
  column = &quot;full&quot;,
  height = 90,
  dpi = 300
)

saved_report &lt;- attr(
  saved_file,
  &quot;figspec_report&quot;
)

loaded_ids
spec_list()[
  spec_list()$id %in% loaded_ids,
  c(&quot;id&quot;, &quot;name&quot;, &quot;publisher&quot;, &quot;origin&quot;)
]
loaded_plot
saved_report[
  saved_report$check %in% c(
    &quot;Width&quot;, &quot;Resolution&quot;, &quot;File format&quot;, &quot;Type size&quot;
  ),
  c(&quot;check&quot;, &quot;requirement&quot;, &quot;actual&quot;, &quot;status&quot;)
]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The YAML file adds research_unit_report as a user-supplied profile. Its 160 mm full width, 300 dpi resolution, PNG format and 9–12 pt type range all pass on the exported time-series figure.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

## Check collections and publication assets

### `submission_check()`

Review figures and tables together

Review figures and tables in one operation. A concise summary identifies each item and shows whether it passes, fails, needs more information or was inspected without a specification. The complete report for every item remains available for closer inspection.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
library(ggplot2)

submission_spec &lt;- spec_get(list(
  name = &quot;Research report figure set&quot;,
  columns = list(single = 85, double = 170),
  height_max_mm = 220,
  dpi_min = 300,
  formats = &quot;png&quot;,
  font_min_pt = 9,
  font_max_pt = 12,
  colour_mode = &quot;RGB&quot;,
  max_file_mb = 20,
  not_stated = c(
    &quot;font_families&quot;, &quot;min_line_pt&quot;, &quot;max_line_pt&quot;,
    &quot;avoid_colour_pairs&quot;, &quot;print_greyscale&quot;
  )
))

vehicles_plot &lt;- ggplot(
  mpg,
  aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv, shape = drv)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = &quot;Vehicle fuel economy&quot;,
    x = &quot;Engine displacement (litres)&quot;,
    y = &quot;Highway fuel economy&quot;,
    colour = &quot;Drive layout&quot;,
    shape = &quot;Drive layout&quot;
  ) +
  fig_apply_spec(submission_spec, base_size = 10)

economy_plot &lt;- ggplot(
  economics,
  aes(date, unemploy)
) +
  geom_line(colour = &quot;#1B4965&quot;, linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = &quot;Unemployment over time&quot;,
    x = NULL,
    y = &quot;People unemployed (thousands)&quot;
  ) +
  fig_apply_spec(
    submission_spec,
    colour = FALSE,
    shapes = FALSE,
    base_size = 10
  )

diamonds_plot &lt;- ggplot(
  diamonds,
  aes(carat, fill = cut)
) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, position = &quot;identity&quot;, alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = &quot;Distribution of diamond size&quot;,
    x = &quot;Carat&quot;,
    y = &quot;Number of diamonds&quot;,
    fill = &quot;Cut&quot;
  ) +
  fig_apply_spec(submission_spec, base_size = 10)

figures &lt;- list(
  vehicles = vehicles_plot,
  economy = economy_plot,
  diamonds = diamonds_plot
)
column_map &lt;- c(
  vehicles = &quot;single&quot;,
  economy = &quot;double&quot;,
  diamonds = &quot;double&quot;
)
file_column_map &lt;- setNames(
  unname(column_map),
  paste0(names(column_map), &quot;.png&quot;)
)

example_root &lt;- tempfile(&quot;figspec-submission-&quot;)
dir.create(example_root)

save_figure_set &lt;- function(directory) {
  dir.create(directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  paths &lt;- vapply(names(figures), function(figure_name) {
    fig_save(
      file.path(directory, paste0(figure_name, &quot;.png&quot;)),
      figures[[figure_name]],
      spec = submission_spec,
      column = unname(column_map[[figure_name]]),
      height = if (figure_name == &quot;vehicles&quot;) 75 else 95,
      dpi = 300,
      check = FALSE
    )
  }, character(1))
  unname(paths)
}
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>x</code></td><td>A non-empty list of supported live figures or tables, a directory path, or a character vector of exported asset paths.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a named list of live figures and tables, one directory, or a character vector of saved-file paths. The example checks three plots containing 234, 574 and 53,940 observations, exports them at their assigned widths and then checks the written files as a second, complementary review.</p><pre><code class="language-r">plot_review &lt;- submission_check(
  figures,
  spec = submission_spec,
  column = column_map,
  dpi = 300
)

submission_directory &lt;- file.path(
  example_root,
  &quot;complete-set&quot;
)
saved_files &lt;- save_figure_set(
  submission_directory
)

file_review &lt;- submission_check(
  saved_files,
  spec = submission_spec,
  column = file_column_map
)

plot_review
file_review</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Both reviews contain one row for each of the three figures. The plot review can assess typography, colour and panel geometry; the file review confirms the actual dimensions, resolution, PNG format, validity and file size.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>The specification to use: a registry id, a figspec_spec, a named list of requirements, or NULL to inspect without assigning pass or fail results.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a bundled registry id, an existing specification or a named list of requirements. Leave it as NULL when you only want an inventory of measurable properties and do not want pass or fail decisions.</p><pre><code class="language-r">specified_review &lt;- submission_check(
  figures,
  spec = submission_spec,
  column = column_map,
  dpi = 300
)

inspection_only &lt;- submission_check(
  figures
)

list(
  against_specification = specified_review,
  inspection_only = inspection_only
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The first review compares every figure with the project specification. The second reports what figspec can measure without claiming that anything passes or fails.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>column</code></td><td>Which named width each figure targets. Supply one non-empty name for the whole set, or a uniquely named character vector covering every figure name in x.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Use one width name when every figure has the same target, or provide a named character vector when figures occupy different widths. Every name must match a figure exactly so a typo cannot silently assign the wrong width.</p><pre><code class="language-r">one_width_review &lt;- submission_check(
  figures,
  spec = submission_spec,
  column = &quot;double&quot;,
  dpi = 300
)

mapped_width_review &lt;- submission_check(
  figures,
  spec = submission_spec,
  column = column_map,
  dpi = 300
)

one_width_review[, c(&quot;file&quot;, &quot;column&quot;)]
mapped_width_review[, c(&quot;file&quot;, &quot;column&quot;)]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The first review assigns double to all three figures. The named mapping assigns single to vehicles and double to economy and diamonds.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>dpi</code></td><td>The shared resolution of files that do not record it themselves. It is also the intended export resolution when x contains live plots.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Provide the shared resolution when a saved raster does not record it. figspec uses the supplied value to convert pixels into physical size; it does not rewrite or resample the file.</p><pre><code class="language-r">png_without_dpi &lt;- file.path(
  example_root,
  &quot;pixels-without-resolution.png&quot;
)
grDevices::png(
  png_without_dpi,
  width = round(85 / 25.4 * 300),
  height = 800
)
print(vehicles_plot)
grDevices::dev.off()

unresolved_dpi &lt;- submission_check(
  png_without_dpi,
  spec = submission_spec,
  column = &quot;single&quot;
)
supplied_dpi &lt;- submission_check(
  png_without_dpi,
  spec = submission_spec,
  column = &quot;single&quot;,
  dpi = 300
)

list(
  without_dpi = submission_detail(
    unresolved_dpi,
    basename(png_without_dpi)
  ),
  with_dpi = submission_detail(
    supplied_dpi,
    basename(png_without_dpi)
  )
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Without a recorded or supplied resolution, the file's physical width and resolution remain unresolved. Supplying 300 dpi allows its 1,004 pixels to be interpreted as approximately 85 mm and both checks pass.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>pattern</code></td><td>Regular expression selecting files when x is a directory. Defaults to common figure and table extensions.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>When x is a directory, use a regular expression to select the files to check. Matching is case-insensitive. Files that do not match remain untouched and are not included in the result.</p><pre><code class="language-r">pattern_directory &lt;- file.path(
  example_root,
  &quot;pattern-selection&quot;
)
save_figure_set(pattern_directory)
writeLines(
  &quot;Supporting notes&quot;,
  file.path(pattern_directory, &quot;README.txt&quot;)
)

pattern_review &lt;- submission_check(
  pattern_directory,
  spec = submission_spec,
  column = &quot;single&quot;,
  pattern = &quot;^vehicles[.]png$&quot;
)

pattern_review[, c(&quot;file&quot;, &quot;column&quot;, &quot;result&quot;)]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Only vehicles.png is selected. The other PNG figures and README.txt remain in the directory but are not checked.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>recursive</code></td><td>Whether a directory scan should include subdirectories. Must be one TRUE or FALSE value.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Set recursive to TRUE when figures are organised in subdirectories. FALSE checks only the selected directory itself; TRUE also checks matching files below it.</p><pre><code class="language-r">recursive_directory &lt;- file.path(
  example_root,
  &quot;recursive-selection&quot;
)
nested_directory &lt;- file.path(
  recursive_directory,
  &quot;supplement&quot;
)
dir.create(
  nested_directory,
  recursive = TRUE
)

fig_save(
  file.path(recursive_directory, &quot;main.png&quot;),
  vehicles_plot,
  spec = submission_spec,
  column = &quot;single&quot;,
  height = 75,
  dpi = 300,
  check = FALSE
)
fig_save(
  file.path(nested_directory, &quot;supplement.png&quot;),
  economy_plot,
  spec = submission_spec,
  column = &quot;single&quot;,
  height = 75,
  dpi = 300,
  check = FALSE
)

top_level_only &lt;- submission_check(
  recursive_directory,
  spec = submission_spec,
  column = &quot;single&quot;,
  recursive = FALSE
)
including_nested &lt;- submission_check(
  recursive_directory,
  spec = submission_spec,
  column = &quot;single&quot;,
  recursive = TRUE
)

list(
  top_level_only = top_level_only,
  including_nested = including_nested
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The non-recursive review contains main.png only. The recursive review contains both main.png and the supplementary figure stored one directory below it.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>art_type</code></td><td>Resolution category passed to fig_check(). &quot;auto&quot; uses the content of a live plot; for saved files, where that evidence has been lost, it applies the strictest recorded threshold. Explicit choices are &quot;colour&quot;, &quot;bw&quot;, &quot;line&quot; and &quot;combination&quot;.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Choose which resolution rule applies when the artwork type is already known. Auto examines live plots; an explicit value is useful when the same visual content will be delivered as colour artwork, black and white artwork, line art or a combination.</p><pre><code class="language-r">cell_plot &lt;- ggplot(
  mpg,
  aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv, shape = drv)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  fig_apply_spec(&quot;cell_press&quot;)

colour_review &lt;- submission_check(
  list(figure = cell_plot),
  spec = &quot;cell_press&quot;,
  column = &quot;single&quot;,
  dpi = 300,
  art_type = &quot;colour&quot;
)
line_art_review &lt;- submission_check(
  list(figure = cell_plot),
  spec = &quot;cell_press&quot;,
  column = &quot;single&quot;,
  dpi = 300,
  art_type = &quot;line&quot;
)

colour_resolution &lt;- submission_detail(
  colour_review,
  &quot;figure&quot;
)
colour_resolution &lt;- colour_resolution[
  colour_resolution$check == &quot;Resolution&quot;,
]
line_resolution &lt;- submission_detail(
  line_art_review,
  &quot;figure&quot;
)
line_resolution &lt;- line_resolution[
  line_resolution$check == &quot;Resolution&quot;,
]

rbind(
  colour = colour_resolution,
  line_art = line_resolution
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> At 300 dpi the colour interpretation passes Cell Press's 300 dpi rule, while the line-art interpretation fails its stricter 1,000 dpi rule.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>asset_type</code></td><td>Whether each item is a figure or table. The default detects live objects and treats HTML, DOCX, RTF and TeX files as tables. A uniquely named vector can classify every item explicitly.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Leave asset_type as auto for ordinary use. figspec recognises supported live figures and tables and recognises HTML, DOCX, RTF and TeX files as tables. Name each value when an image or PDF contains a table and the file type alone cannot reveal that.</p><pre><code class="language-r">mixed_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Research report&quot;,
  columns = list(single = 85),
  dpi_min = 300,
  formats = &quot;png&quot;,
  tables = list(
    font_min_pt = 9,
    header_bold = TRUE
  )
)
mixed_review &lt;- submission_check(
  list(
    figure = vehicles_plot,
    table = head(mpg)
  ),
  spec = mixed_spec,
  column = &quot;single&quot;,
  asset_type = &quot;auto&quot;
)

mixed_review[, c(&quot;file&quot;, &quot;asset&quot;, &quot;result&quot;)]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The summary identifies the ggplot as a figure and the data frame as a table, then sends each item through the checks that apply to that kind of asset.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `submission_detail()`

Open the full report for one submission item

A collection review is intentionally brief. Open one figure or table's full report when you need to see why it failed, which values were measured or which requirements could not be assessed. This example checks two plots made from all 234 rows of ggplot2's mpg data. The second plot deliberately uses text below the project's minimum so there is a real problem to diagnose.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
library(ggplot2)

detail_spec &lt;- spec_get(list(
  name = &quot;Research report&quot;,
  columns = list(single = 85),
  dpi_min = 300,
  formats = &quot;png&quot;,
  font_min_pt = 9,
  font_max_pt = 12,
  colour_mode = &quot;RGB&quot;,
  not_stated = c(
    &quot;font_families&quot;, &quot;min_line_pt&quot;, &quot;max_line_pt&quot;,
    &quot;avoid_colour_pairs&quot;, &quot;print_greyscale&quot;
  )
))

ready_plot &lt;- ggplot(
  mpg,
  aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv, shape = drv)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = &quot;Vehicle fuel economy&quot;,
    x = &quot;Engine displacement (litres)&quot;,
    y = &quot;Highway fuel economy&quot;,
    colour = &quot;Drive layout&quot;,
    shape = &quot;Drive layout&quot;
  ) +
  fig_apply_spec(detail_spec, base_size = 10)

small_text_plot &lt;- ready_plot +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 7),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 7),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 7)
  )

detail_review &lt;- submission_check(
  list(
    ready = ready_plot,
    text_too_small = small_text_plot
  ),
  spec = detail_spec,
  column = &quot;single&quot;,
  dpi = 300
)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>x</code></td><td>The complete figspec_submission object returned by submission_check().<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Pass the complete result from submission_check(). Keep that object intact: it contains the short summary you can see and the full report stored for each figure or table.</p><pre><code class="language-r">ready_detail &lt;- submission_detail(
  x = detail_review,
  file = &quot;ready&quot;
)

ready_detail</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The full report for ready lists every requirement that figspec assessed, including width, resolution, typography, colour and panel geometry.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>file</code></td><td>Exactly one item name from the file column of x. For live objects this is the list name; for saved assets it is the file name shown in the submission summary.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Choose one name exactly as it appears in the summary's file column. For a named list this is the item name; for saved figures or tables it is the displayed file name.</p><pre><code class="language-r">problem_detail &lt;- submission_detail(
  detail_review,
  file = &quot;text_too_small&quot;
)

problem_detail[
  problem_detail$status == &quot;fail&quot;,
  c(&quot;check&quot;, &quot;requirement&quot;, &quot;actual&quot;, &quot;status&quot;)
]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The detailed report identifies Type size as the failed check, records the required 9–12 pt range and shows that the smallest text is 7 pt.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `fig_suggest_art_type()`

Choose a resolution category for a figure

Resolution requirements depend on the kind of artwork being exported. Run the setup once, then use these examples to see how figspec classifies a real plot and how a publication or project specification supplies the thresholds needed to make the final choice.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
library(ggplot2)

colour_plot &lt;- ggplot(
  mpg,
  aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv, shape = drv)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_figspec(&quot;okabe_ito&quot;) +
  labs(
    x = &quot;Engine displacement (litres)&quot;,
    y = &quot;Highway fuel economy&quot;,
    colour = &quot;Drive layout&quot;,
    shape = &quot;Drive layout&quot;
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

resolution_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Research report&quot;,
  dpi_min = 300,
  dpi_bw = 600,
  dpi_line_art = 1000,
  dpi_combination = 600
)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>plot</code></td><td>A ggplot object.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Pass the ggplot object before exporting it. figspec examines the marks, fills and colours that the plot will draw; it does not infer the category from the function names used to build the plot.</p><pre><code class="language-r">suggested_type &lt;- fig_suggest_art_type(
  plot = colour_plot
)

suggested_type</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The function returns &quot;colour&quot; because the plot uses coloured points. That value can be passed to fig_check() or fig_save() as art_type = &quot;colour&quot;.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>Optional specification: a registry id, a figspec_spec, or a named list of requirements. When supplied, its resolution thresholds are shown alongside the suggestion.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a bundled registry id or your own specification when you also want to see the available resolution thresholds. The argument keeps its original name for compatibility and is not limited to journals.</p><pre><code class="language-r">suggested_with_rules &lt;- fig_suggest_art_type(
  colour_plot,
  spec = resolution_spec
)

# A bundled profile works in the same position:
# fig_suggest_art_type(colour_plot, spec = &quot;cell_press&quot;)

suggested_with_rules</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The plot is still classified as colour, and the report also shows the project's 300 dpi colour, 600 dpi greyscale and combination, and 1,000 dpi line-art thresholds.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `fig_refit()`

Re-export a figure set for a new specification

Use this function when a complete set of editable plots must be prepared for a new destination. The examples use 234 vehicle observations and 574 monthly economic observations, export real files and then inspect the resulting submission report. The destination can be a journal, report, organisation or any other recorded specification.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
library(ggplot2)

vehicle_plot &lt;- ggplot(
  mpg,
  aes(displ, hwy, colour = drv, shape = drv)
) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_figspec(&quot;okabe_ito&quot;) +
  labs(
    title = &quot;Vehicle fuel economy&quot;,
    x = &quot;Engine displacement (litres)&quot;,
    y = &quot;Highway fuel economy&quot;,
    colour = &quot;Drive layout&quot;,
    shape = &quot;Drive layout&quot;
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

economy_plot &lt;- ggplot(
  economics,
  aes(date, unemploy)
) +
  geom_line(colour = &quot;#1B4965&quot;, linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = &quot;Unemployment over time&quot;,
    x = NULL,
    y = &quot;People unemployed (thousands)&quot;
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

refit_plots &lt;- list(
  vehicles = vehicle_plot,
  economy = economy_plot
)

handoff_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Research report&quot;,
  columns = list(compact = 85, full = 170),
  dpi_min = 300,
  formats = c(&quot;png&quot;, &quot;tiff&quot;),
  font_min_pt = 9,
  font_max_pt = 12,
  colour_mode = &quot;RGB&quot;,
  not_stated = c(
    &quot;font_families&quot;, &quot;min_line_pt&quot;, &quot;max_line_pt&quot;,
    &quot;avoid_colour_pairs&quot;, &quot;print_greyscale&quot;
  )
)

refit_root &lt;- tempfile(&quot;figspec-refit-&quot;)
dir.create(refit_root)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>plots</code></td><td>A non-empty named list of editable figures. Supported inputs include ggplot2 and patchwork objects, lattice and Plotly plots, grid grobs, and base-graphics code wrapped in functions or one-sided formulas. Names become file stems and must be unique and safe to use as file names.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a named list of live plots. The names become file names, while keeping the plots editable allows figspec to adjust typography before creating new files.</p><pre><code class="language-r">plot_set_review &lt;- fig_refit(
  plots = refit_plots,
  spec = handoff_spec,
  output_dir = file.path(refit_root, &quot;plot-set&quot;),
  column = &quot;full&quot;,
  format = &quot;png&quot;
)

plot_set_review</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Two checked PNG files, vehicles.png and economy.png, are written from the original plot objects at the specification's 170 mm full width.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>The new specification: a registry id, a figspec_spec, or a named list of requirements.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Select the new destination by registry id or pass a project or organisational specification directly. The same specification is used to retheme, size, export and check every plot.</p><pre><code class="language-r">project_review &lt;- fig_refit(
  list(vehicles = vehicle_plot),
  spec = handoff_spec,
  output_dir = file.path(refit_root, &quot;project-specification&quot;),
  column = &quot;compact&quot;,
  format = &quot;png&quot;
)

# A bundled profile works in the same position:
# spec = &quot;pnas&quot;

project_review</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The figure is prepared against the supplied Research report specification rather than a bundled journal profile.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>output_dir</code></td><td>One directory to write into. It is created if necessary.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Choose a dedicated output directory for the new figure set. figspec creates it when necessary and writes each plot under its list name.</p><pre><code class="language-r">new_directory &lt;- file.path(
  refit_root,
  &quot;report-ready&quot;
)
directory_review &lt;- fig_refit(
  list(vehicles = vehicle_plot),
  handoff_spec,
  output_dir = new_directory,
  column = &quot;compact&quot;,
  format = &quot;png&quot;
)

list(
  review = directory_review,
  files = list.files(new_directory)
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The new directory contains vehicles.png, and the returned review records the checks performed on that exact file.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>column</code></td><td>Which column width to use, either one value for all plots or a uniquely named vector mapping every plot name to a width.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Use one width name for every plot or provide a named mapping when the figures occupy different amounts of space. Every mapping name must match a plot name exactly.</p><pre><code class="language-r">mapped_review &lt;- fig_refit(
  refit_plots,
  handoff_spec,
  output_dir = file.path(refit_root, &quot;mixed-widths&quot;),
  column = c(
    vehicles = &quot;compact&quot;,
    economy = &quot;full&quot;
  ),
  format = &quot;png&quot;
)

mapped_review[, c(&quot;file&quot;, &quot;column&quot;, &quot;result&quot;)]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> vehicles.png is exported at the 85 mm compact width and economy.png at the 170 mm full width; the returned rows preserve that mapping.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>retheme</code></td><td>Whether to apply the requirements exposed by each plotting system before export. Must be one TRUE or FALSE.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Leave this TRUE to apply the new specification's typography before export. Set it to FALSE only when the plots have already been styled correctly and you want figspec to preserve that styling unchanged.</p><pre><code class="language-r">themed_review &lt;- fig_refit(
  list(vehicles = vehicle_plot),
  handoff_spec,
  output_dir = file.path(refit_root, &quot;with-retheming&quot;),
  column = &quot;compact&quot;,
  retheme = TRUE,
  format = &quot;png&quot;
)
unchanged_review &lt;- suppressWarnings(
  fig_refit(
    list(vehicles = vehicle_plot),
    handoff_spec,
    output_dir = file.path(refit_root, &quot;without-retheming&quot;),
    column = &quot;compact&quot;,
    retheme = FALSE,
    format = &quot;png&quot;
  )
)

themed_type &lt;- submission_detail(
  themed_review,
  &quot;vehicles.png&quot;
)
themed_type &lt;- themed_type[
  themed_type$check == &quot;Type size&quot;,
]
unchanged_type &lt;- submission_detail(
  unchanged_review,
  &quot;vehicles.png&quot;
)
unchanged_type &lt;- unchanged_type[
  unchanged_type$check == &quot;Type size&quot;,
]

rbind(
  rethemed = themed_type,
  unchanged = unchanged_type
)[, c(&quot;check&quot;, &quot;requirement&quot;, &quot;actual&quot;, &quot;status&quot;)]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Retheming brings the plot into the required 9–12 pt range. Preserving the original 14 pt theme leaves a Type size failure visible in the second report.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>format</code></td><td>File extension without a dot. Defaults to the first writable format accepted by the specification.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a file extension without a dot when you need a particular accepted format. If it is omitted, figspec chooses the first format in the specification that R can write reliably.</p><pre><code class="language-r">png_review &lt;- fig_refit(
  list(economy = economy_plot),
  handoff_spec,
  output_dir = file.path(refit_root, &quot;explicit-format&quot;),
  column = &quot;full&quot;,
  format = &quot;png&quot;
)

png_review[, c(&quot;file&quot;, &quot;result&quot;)]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The exported file is named economy.png and its detailed report confirms that PNG is accepted by the specification.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `media_spec()`

Look up supplementary media requirements

Video and audio files have requirements that ordinary figure checks cannot assess. Use this lookup to see the accepted containers, frame limits, codec, bit rate and file-size rules recorded for a publication or project.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
project_media_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Research media handoff&quot;,
  source_url = &quot;internal:media-guide&quot;,
  verified_on = as.character(Sys.Date()),
  media = list(
    video_formats = &quot;mp4&quot;,
    video_codec = &quot;h264&quot;,
    frame_max = list(width = 1280, height = 720),
    max_file_mb = 5
  )
)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>A registry id such as &quot;science&quot;, a figspec_spec, or a named list of requirements.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a bundled registry id or your own specification. If no media rules are recorded, figspec says so instead of treating the absence of data as permission to use any format.</p><pre><code class="language-r">science_media_rules &lt;- media_spec(
  spec = &quot;science&quot;
)
project_media_rules &lt;- media_spec(
  spec = project_media_spec
)

list(
  publication = science_media_rules,
  project = project_media_rules
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The two lookups return their stated formats, frame limits and other media rules, each with the specification name, source and date last checked.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `media_check()`

Verify a supplementary media file

These examples create a real 640 × 360 pixel MP4, read it back from disk and compare its saved properties with a media specification. ffprobe adds codec and bit-rate inspection when it is installed; properties that cannot be read are reported as unknown rather than guessed.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
ffmpeg &lt;- Sys.which(&quot;ffmpeg&quot;)
if (!nzchar(ffmpeg)) {
  stop(&quot;This example requires FFmpeg.&quot;)
}

media_file &lt;- tempfile(fileext = &quot;.mp4&quot;)
ffmpeg_output &lt;- system2(
  ffmpeg,
  c(
    &quot;-loglevel&quot;, &quot;error&quot;, &quot;-y&quot;,
    &quot;-f&quot;, &quot;lavfi&quot;, &quot;-i&quot;,
    &quot;color=c=0x1B4965:s=640x360:d=0.5&quot;,
    &quot;-c:v&quot;, &quot;libx264&quot;,
    &quot;-pix_fmt&quot;, &quot;yuv420p&quot;,
    media_file
  ),
  stdout = TRUE,
  stderr = TRUE
)
if (!is.null(attr(ffmpeg_output, &quot;status&quot;))) {
  stop(&quot;FFmpeg could not create the example video.&quot;)
}

video_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Research media handoff&quot;,
  source_url = &quot;internal:media-guide&quot;,
  verified_on = as.character(Sys.Date()),
  media = list(
    video_formats = &quot;mp4&quot;,
    video_codec = &quot;h264&quot;,
    frame_max = list(width = 1280, height = 720),
    max_file_mb = 5
  )
)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>path</code></td><td>One path to an existing media file.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Pass one existing media file. figspec inspects the actual file rather than trusting its extension, so a damaged or incorrectly named file is reported as invalid.</p><pre><code class="language-r">media_report &lt;- media_check(
  path = media_file,
  spec = video_spec
)

media_report</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The saved MP4 is opened and reported as a valid 640 × 360 H.264 file below the 1,280 × 720 frame limit and 5 MB size limit.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>A registry id, a figspec_spec, or a named list containing supplementary media requirements.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Select the media requirements by registry id or pass a project or organisational specification. Only the media part of the specification is used for this check.</p><pre><code class="language-r">project_media_report &lt;- media_check(
  media_file,
  spec = video_spec
)

# A bundled profile works in the same position:
science_media_report &lt;- media_check(
  media_file,
  spec = &quot;science&quot;
)

list(
  project = project_media_report,
  publication = science_media_report
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Both reports inspect the same real file, but each applies the formats, codec, frame limit and file-size rule recorded by its own specification.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `graphical_abstract_spec()`

Look up graphical abstract requirements

A graphical abstract may have a different canvas, resolution, format and text limit from the figures inside the article or report. This function retrieves those separate requirements without mixing them into an ordinary figure check.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
project_abstract_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Research summary card&quot;,
  source_url = &quot;internal:summary-card-guide&quot;,
  verified_on = as.character(Sys.Date()),
  graphical_abstract = list(
    width_mm = 120,
    height_mm = 70,
    dpi_min = 300,
    formats = &quot;png&quot;,
    max_characters = 180
  )
)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>A registry id such as &quot;rsc&quot;, a figspec_spec, or a named list containing graphical-abstract requirements.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a bundled registry id or your own specification. If the selected profile has no graphical-abstract rules on record, figspec reports the gap instead of borrowing ordinary figure dimensions.</p><pre><code class="language-r">rsc_abstract_rules &lt;- graphical_abstract_spec(
  spec = &quot;rsc&quot;
)
project_abstract_rules &lt;- graphical_abstract_spec(
  spec = project_abstract_spec
)

list(
  publication = rsc_abstract_rules,
  project = project_abstract_rules
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The RSC profile returns its 80 × 40 mm graphical-abstract size and 250-character limit; the project profile returns its separate 120 × 70 mm PNG specification.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

## Build, export and check tables

### `table_spec()`

Look up table requirements

Retrieve the table requirements recorded for a publication, project or organisation. Measurable fields can be passed directly to the table build, export and check workflow; editorial instructions remain visible for review with the same source and review date.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
custom_table_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Annual research report&quot;,
  source_url = &quot;internal:report-style-guide&quot;,
  verified_on = as.character(Sys.Date()),
  tables = list(
    orientation = &quot;portrait&quot;,
    title_style = &quot;Short title above the table&quot;,
    notes = &quot;Define abbreviations below the table&quot;
  )
)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>A registry id such as &quot;nature&quot;, a figspec_spec, or a named list containing table requirements.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a bundled registry id or a specification maintained by your project or organisation. The returned object contains only the table instructions, together with their source and review date.</p><pre><code class="language-r">nature_table_rules &lt;- table_spec(
  spec = &quot;nature&quot;
)
report_table_rules &lt;- table_spec(
  spec = custom_table_spec
)

list(
  publication = nature_table_rules,
  project = report_table_rules
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The publication lookup returns Nature's recorded table instructions, while the project lookup returns the portrait orientation, title placement and abbreviation note defined in the local specification.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `table_apply_spec()`

Apply a specification to a table

Apply measurable table requirements while the table is still editable. Data frames and matrices become gt tables; gt, flextable, kableExtra and grid tables remain in their own table systems.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
table_project_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Research report&quot;,
  source_url = &quot;internal:report-table-guide&quot;,
  verified_on = as.character(Sys.Date()),
  tables = list(
    formats = c(&quot;html&quot;, &quot;docx&quot;),
    orientation = &quot;portrait&quot;,
    font_families = &quot;Arial&quot;,
    font_min_pt = 9,
    header_bold = TRUE,
    vertical_rules = FALSE,
    horizontal_rules = &quot;minimal&quot;,
    repeat_header = TRUE
  )
)
vehicle_table &lt;- ggplot2::mpg[1:12, c(
  &quot;manufacturer&quot;, &quot;model&quot;, &quot;displ&quot;, &quot;year&quot;, &quot;hwy&quot;
)]
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>table</code></td><td>A supported table object.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a data frame, matrix, gt table, flextable, kableExtra table or grid table. The example uses twelve real vehicle records and keeps all five selected columns.</p><pre><code class="language-r">styled_vehicle_table &lt;- table_apply_spec(
  table = vehicle_table,
  spec = table_project_spec
)

styled_vehicle_table</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The data frame becomes an editable gt table containing the same 12 rows and five columns.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>The specification to apply. It must contain a tables section.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a specification with a tables section. figspec applies the stated type size, font, header emphasis, rules and width where the selected table system exposes them.</p><pre><code class="language-r">styled_for_report &lt;- table_apply_spec(
  vehicle_table,
  spec = table_project_spec
)
table_check(
  styled_for_report,
  spec = table_project_spec
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The live-table report confirms the applied 9 pt type, bold header, minimal horizontal rules and absence of vertical rules; repeated headers remain output-format dependent.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `table_save()`

Export and verify a table

Export a table through its own table system, reopen the completed file and keep the live-object and file checks together. A temporary file is promoted only after the renderer succeeds and, when checking is enabled, the file is confirmed to be structurally valid.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
table_save_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Research report&quot;,
  source_url = &quot;internal:report-table-guide&quot;,
  verified_on = as.character(Sys.Date()),
  tables = list(
    formats = &quot;html&quot;,
    font_min_pt = 9,
    header_bold = TRUE,
    vertical_rules = FALSE
  )
)
table_for_export &lt;- ggplot2::mpg[1:20, c(
  &quot;manufacturer&quot;, &quot;model&quot;, &quot;displ&quot;, &quot;hwy&quot;
)]
table_output_dir &lt;- tempfile(&quot;figspec-table-options-&quot;)
dir.create(table_output_dir)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>filename</code></td><td>Destination file. The extension selects the output format.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Give a path whose extension names the required table format. The example writes into a directory with a space to exercise an ordinary real-world path.</p><pre><code class="language-r">html_table_path &lt;- file.path(
  table_output_dir,
  &quot;vehicle summary.html&quot;
)
saved_html_table &lt;- table_save(
  filename = html_table_path,
  table = table_for_export,
  spec = table_save_spec
)

file.exists(saved_html_table)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> A non-empty HTML table is written at the requested path and TRUE is returned.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>table</code></td><td>A supported table object.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply the editable table object. This example starts from 20 rows of mpg data; the written HTML is then reopened rather than inferred from the input object.</p><pre><code class="language-r">second_table_path &lt;- file.path(
  table_output_dir,
  &quot;second-table.html&quot;
)
saved_second_table &lt;- table_save(
  second_table_path,
  table = table_for_export,
  spec = table_save_spec
)
attr(
  saved_second_table,
  &quot;figspec_table_report&quot;
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The returned report includes a passing HTML format check from the file and styling checks from the editable table.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>The specification to apply and check, or NULL.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Use a bundled or project specification with table requirements. Leave it NULL to export without transforming or assigning compliance decisions.</p><pre><code class="language-r">specified_table_path &lt;- file.path(
  table_output_dir,
  &quot;specified-table.html&quot;
)
specified_table &lt;- table_save(
  specified_table_path,
  table_for_export,
  spec = table_save_spec
)

attr(specified_table, &quot;figspec_table_report&quot;)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The table is styled, exported and checked against the project specification in one call.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>transform</code></td><td>Whether to call table_apply_spec() before export.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>TRUE applies supported requirements before export. FALSE preserves an already prepared table and still allows the completed file to be checked.</p><pre><code class="language-r">prepared_table &lt;- table_apply_spec(
  table_for_export,
  table_save_spec
)
preserved_table_path &lt;- file.path(
  table_output_dir,
  &quot;preserved-table.html&quot;
)
preserved_table &lt;- table_save(
  preserved_table_path,
  prepared_table,
  spec = table_save_spec,
  transform = FALSE
)

attr(preserved_table, &quot;figspec_table_report&quot;)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The existing table styling is preserved and both live and file evidence remain in the report.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>check</code></td><td>Whether to reopen and check the completed file.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>TRUE reopens the completed file and attaches its report. Set FALSE only when export is wanted without verification.</p><pre><code class="language-r">unchecked_table_path &lt;- file.path(
  table_output_dir,
  &quot;unchecked-table.html&quot;
)
unchecked_table &lt;- table_save(
  unchecked_table_path,
  table_for_export,
  spec = table_save_spec,
  check = FALSE
)

is.null(attr(
  unchecked_table,
  &quot;figspec_table_report&quot;
))</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The file is written and TRUE confirms that no report was attached.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>...</code></td><td>Arguments passed to the table system's exporter.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Named extra values are passed to the selected table exporter. Use them only for options understood by that backend.</p><pre><code class="language-r">exporter_table_path &lt;- file.path(
  table_output_dir,
  &quot;exporter-table.html&quot;
)
exporter_table &lt;- table_save(
  exporter_table_path,
  table_for_export,
  spec = table_save_spec,
  inline_css = TRUE
)

file.exists(exporter_table)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The gt exporter receives the named inline-CSS option and writes the HTML table.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `table_check()`

Verify a table against a specification

Check an editable R table or a completed table file. The two inputs retain different evidence, so table_save combines them when both are available.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
table_check_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Research report&quot;,
  source_url = &quot;internal:report-table-guide&quot;,
  verified_on = as.character(Sys.Date()),
  tables = list(
    formats = &quot;html&quot;,
    font_min_pt = 9,
    header_bold = TRUE,
    vertical_rules = FALSE
  )
)
table_check_data &lt;- ggplot2::mpg[1:10, c(
  &quot;manufacturer&quot;, &quot;model&quot;, &quot;displ&quot;, &quot;hwy&quot;
)]
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>x</code></td><td>A supported live table or one table-file path.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a live supported table or one HTML, DOCX, RTF, TeX, PDF, PNG or JPEG path. The example checks a styled table containing ten real rows.</p><pre><code class="language-r">check_ready_table &lt;- table_apply_spec(
  table_check_data,
  table_check_spec
)
live_table_report &lt;- table_check(
  x = check_ready_table,
  spec = table_check_spec
)

live_table_report</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The report verifies the measurable styling retained by the live gt table and leaves the future file format unresolved.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>The specification to use, or NULL for inspection only.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply the table specification used to decide pass, fail and unresolved results. NULL produces an inspection without claiming compliance.</p><pre><code class="language-r">inspection_report &lt;- table_check(
  table_check_data,
  spec = NULL
)
specified_report &lt;- table_check(
  table_apply_spec(
    table_check_data,
    table_check_spec
  ),
  spec = table_check_spec
)

list(
  inspection = inspection_report,
  specified = specified_report
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The inspection has no compliance verdict; the specified check evaluates the requirements that the live table exposes.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

## R Markdown and Quarto

### `figspec_knitr_options()`

Create figure settings for R Markdown or Quarto

Figures created inside R Markdown or Quarto need the same deliberate size and resolution as figures saved from an R script. These examples translate a specification into the four settings knitr uses: figure width, figure height, resolution and graphics device.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
report_chunk_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Research report&quot;,
  columns = list(compact = 85, full = 170),
  formats = &quot;png&quot;,
  dpi_min = 300,
  dpi_line_art = 600
)

slide_chunk_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Presentation slide&quot;,
  formats = &quot;png&quot;,
  dpi_min = 192
)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>The specification to use: a registry id such as &quot;plos_one&quot;, a figspec_spec, or a named list of requirements.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply a bundled registry id or your own project or organisational specification. The returned settings can be applied to one chunk or to the whole document.</p><pre><code class="language-r">report_options &lt;- figspec_knitr_options(
  spec = report_chunk_spec,
  column = &quot;full&quot;
)

# A bundled profile works in the same position:
publication_options &lt;- figspec_knitr_options(
  spec = &quot;plos_one&quot;,
  column = &quot;single&quot;
)

list(
  project = report_options,
  publication = publication_options
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Each specification produces its own width, height, resolution and graphics device settings, ready to pass to knitr.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>column</code></td><td>Which named width in the specification to use. Leave it NULL when supplying width explicitly.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Choose one of the widths named in the specification. figspec converts the recorded millimetres to inches because that is the unit knitr uses for fig.width and fig.height.</p><pre><code class="language-r">compact_options &lt;- figspec_knitr_options(
  report_chunk_spec,
  column = &quot;compact&quot;
)
full_options &lt;- figspec_knitr_options(
  report_chunk_spec,
  column = &quot;full&quot;
)

c(
  compact_width_in = compact_options$fig.width,
  full_width_in = full_options$fig.width
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The 85 mm compact width becomes approximately 3.35 inches and the 170 mm full width becomes approximately 6.69 inches.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>width</code></td><td>Explicit figure width for specifications that do not publish named columns.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply an explicit width when a specification has no named columns or when the output format uses a project-specific canvas. Do not combine width with column.</p><pre><code class="language-r">slide_options &lt;- figspec_knitr_options(
  slide_chunk_spec,
  width = 12,
  height = 6.75,
  units = &quot;in&quot;
)

slide_options</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The presentation figure is configured as a 12 × 6.75 inch PNG at the project's recorded 192 dpi.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>height</code></td><td>Figure height. Defaults to three quarters of the width, which is a convenience rather than a journal requirement.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Set the intended figure height when the default three-quarter aspect ratio is not suitable. The value uses the unit selected by units.</p><pre><code class="language-r">short_options &lt;- figspec_knitr_options(
  report_chunk_spec,
  column = &quot;full&quot;,
  height = 90,
  units = &quot;mm&quot;
)

short_options[c(&quot;fig.width&quot;, &quot;fig.height&quot;)]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The figure remains 170 mm wide and is set to exactly 90 mm high, expressed to knitr as approximately 6.69 × 3.54 inches.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>units</code></td><td>Units for width and height.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>State whether explicit width and height values are millimetres, centimetres or inches. The returned chunk dimensions are always in inches because knitr requires them that way.</p><pre><code class="language-r">centimetre_options &lt;- figspec_knitr_options(
  slide_chunk_spec,
  width = 16,
  height = 9,
  units = &quot;cm&quot;
)

centimetre_options[c(&quot;fig.width&quot;, &quot;fig.height&quot;)]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> A 16 × 9 cm request becomes approximately 6.30 × 3.54 inches without changing the intended physical size.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>art_type</code></td><td>Resolution category.
