With no plot available, &quot;auto&quot; conservatively uses the strictest rule the journal states.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Choose the resolution category when the document setup already knows what kind of artwork its chunks will produce. With &quot;auto&quot;, no plot is available yet, so figspec uses the strictest recorded threshold.</p><pre><code class="language-r">colour_options &lt;- figspec_knitr_options(
  report_chunk_spec,
  column = &quot;full&quot;,
  art_type = &quot;colour&quot;
)
line_options &lt;- figspec_knitr_options(
  report_chunk_spec,
  column = &quot;full&quot;,
  art_type = &quot;line&quot;
)

c(
  colour_dpi = colour_options$dpi,
  line_dpi = line_options$dpi
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Colour output uses the recorded 300 dpi minimum, while line art uses the stricter 600 dpi requirement.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `figspec_knitr_setup()`

Apply figure settings to R Markdown or Quarto

Use this function once in a document's setup chunk to make the chosen figure settings the defaults for later chunks. Each example applies the settings and then reads them back from knitr so the effect is visible.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
if (!requireNamespace(&quot;knitr&quot;, quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop(&quot;This example requires knitr.&quot;)
}

document_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Research report&quot;,
  columns = list(compact = 85, full = 170),
  formats = &quot;png&quot;,
  dpi_min = 300,
  dpi_line_art = 600
)

presentation_spec &lt;- list(
  name = &quot;Presentation slide&quot;,
  formats = &quot;png&quot;,
  dpi_min = 192
)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>spec</code></td><td>The specification to use: a registry id such as &quot;plos_one&quot;, a figspec_spec, or a named list of requirements.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply the publication, project or organisational specification that should govern figures in the document. The argument retains its original name for compatibility.</p><pre><code class="language-r">figspec_knitr_setup(
  spec = document_spec,
  column = &quot;full&quot;
)

knitr::opts_chunk$get(
  c(&quot;fig.width&quot;, &quot;fig.height&quot;, &quot;dpi&quot;, &quot;dev&quot;)
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The current knitr session now uses the Research report's full width, strictest recorded resolution and PNG device as its defaults.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>column</code></td><td>Which named width in the specification to use. Leave it NULL when supplying width explicitly.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Choose which named width later chunks should use by default. Changing this value updates the physical figure width for the whole document.</p><pre><code class="language-r">figspec_knitr_setup(
  document_spec,
  column = &quot;compact&quot;
)
compact_width &lt;- knitr::opts_chunk$get(&quot;fig.width&quot;)

figspec_knitr_setup(
  document_spec,
  column = &quot;full&quot;
)
full_width &lt;- knitr::opts_chunk$get(&quot;fig.width&quot;)

c(compact = compact_width, full = full_width)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The defaults change from approximately 3.35 inches for compact figures to 6.69 inches for full-width figures.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>width</code></td><td>Explicit figure width for specifications that do not publish named columns.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Set an explicit document-wide width when the specification does not provide named columns. Leave column unset when using this argument.</p><pre><code class="language-r">figspec_knitr_setup(
  presentation_spec,
  width = 10,
  height = 5.625,
  units = &quot;in&quot;
)

knitr::opts_chunk$get(
  c(&quot;fig.width&quot;, &quot;fig.height&quot;, &quot;dpi&quot;)
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Later chunks use a 10 × 5.625 inch canvas at the presentation specification's 192 dpi.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>height</code></td><td>Figure height. Defaults to three quarters of the width, which is a convenience rather than a journal requirement.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Set a document-wide figure height when the default aspect ratio is not appropriate for the report or presentation layout.</p><pre><code class="language-r">figspec_knitr_setup(
  document_spec,
  column = &quot;full&quot;,
  height = 90,
  units = &quot;mm&quot;
)

knitr::opts_chunk$get(
  c(&quot;fig.width&quot;, &quot;fig.height&quot;)
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Later chunks default to figures measuring 170 × 90 mm, represented internally by knitr in inches.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>units</code></td><td>Units for width and height.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>State the unit used by explicit width and height values. This lets a presentation use inches while a report specification continues to use millimetres or centimetres.</p><pre><code class="language-r">figspec_knitr_setup(
  presentation_spec,
  width = 12,
  height = 6.75,
  units = &quot;in&quot;
)

knitr::opts_chunk$get(
  c(&quot;fig.width&quot;, &quot;fig.height&quot;)
)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The active defaults become exactly 12 × 6.75 inches.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>art_type</code></td><td>Resolution category. With no plot available, &quot;auto&quot; conservatively uses the strictest rule the journal states.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Select the resolution category that should apply to later chunks. Use an explicit category when all figures in the document share that kind of artwork; otherwise set it on individual chunks as needed.</p><pre><code class="language-r">figspec_knitr_setup(
  document_spec,
  column = &quot;full&quot;,
  art_type = &quot;colour&quot;
)
colour_dpi &lt;- knitr::opts_chunk$get(&quot;dpi&quot;)

figspec_knitr_setup(
  document_spec,
  column = &quot;full&quot;,
  art_type = &quot;line&quot;
)
line_dpi &lt;- knitr::opts_chunk$get(&quot;dpi&quot;)

c(colour = colour_dpi, line = line_dpi)</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The document default changes from 300 dpi for colour figures to 600 dpi for line art.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

## Maintain trusted registry data

### `registry_status()`

Review registry coverage and update dates

Use this summary to see when every specification was last checked and how much of its field list has been reviewed. It distinguishes a requirement recorded from the source, a field reviewed but not stated, and a field that still needs review.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
today &lt;- Sys.Date()
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>max_age_days</code></td><td>Age beyond which an entry is flagged for rechecking. Defaults to 365.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Choose how old a review may be before it is flagged. This changes only the stale indicator; it does not remove or alter any specification.</p><pre><code class="language-r">annual_review_status &lt;- registry_status(
  max_age_days = 365,
  as_of = today
)

annual_review_status[
  order(annual_review_status$age_days, decreasing = TRUE),
  c(&quot;id&quot;, &quot;verified_on&quot;, &quot;age_days&quot;, &quot;stale&quot;)
]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> Every registry profile is listed with its review date and age, and profiles older than 365 days are marked for attention.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>as_of</code></td><td>One Date to measure against. Defaults to today.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply the date from which ages should be calculated. The default is today; an explicit date is useful for reproducible reports and tests.</p><pre><code class="language-r">dated_status &lt;- registry_status(
  max_age_days = 365,
  as_of = as.Date(&quot;2026-09-05&quot;)
)

dated_status[
  , c(
    &quot;id&quot;, &quot;verified_on&quot;, &quot;age_days&quot;, &quot;stale&quot;,
    &quot;stated&quot;, &quot;confirmed_absent&quot;, &quot;unharvested&quot;
  )
]</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The age and stale columns are calculated as they stood on 5 September 2026, while the three coverage columns account for every supported requirement field.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `registry_stale_entries()`

Find specifications due for review

Use this focused check when you want the ids of specifications whose source pages are due to be reviewed again. It reports the entries and returns their ids so they can be passed into an updating workflow.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
today &lt;- Sys.Date()
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>max_age_days</code></td><td>Age beyond which an entry is flagged for rechecking. Defaults to 365.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Set the maximum acceptable age in days. A shorter interval produces a larger review list; a longer interval limits the result to older records.</p><pre><code class="language-r">due_for_quarterly_review &lt;- registry_stale_entries(
  max_age_days = 90,
  as_of = today
)

due_for_quarterly_review</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The function reports profiles more than 90 days old and invisibly returns their registry ids for follow-up.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>as_of</code></td><td>One Date to measure against. Defaults to today.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Set the date against which review ages are measured. Using an explicit date makes a maintenance report reproducible.</p><pre><code class="language-r">due_on_review_date &lt;- registry_stale_entries(
  max_age_days = 90,
  as_of = as.Date(&quot;2026-09-05&quot;)
)

due_on_review_date</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The returned ids are those whose last review was more than 90 days before 5 September 2026.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `registry_check_sources()`

Check whether registry source pages still respond

A stored source address can stop working even when the registry file itself has not changed. This function asks the selected pages whether they still respond and separates missing pages from temporary failures, redirects and sites that block automated requests. It requires an internet connection.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
# No setup is required. The examples make live network requests.
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>ids</code></td><td>Character vector of registry ids to check. Defaults to all of them.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Supply one or more registry ids when you want to check selected source pages. Leave this NULL to review every bundled profile.</p><pre><code class="language-r">selected_sources &lt;- registry_check_sources(
  ids = c(&quot;plos_one&quot;, &quot;cell_press&quot;),
  timeout = 10
)

selected_sources</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> One row is returned for each selected profile, with the original address, HTTP status, verdict and any final address reached after redirection.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>timeout</code></td><td>One positive number giving the seconds allowed for each response.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Set how many seconds each source request may take. A larger value can help with slow publisher sites but also makes a full registry review take longer.</p><pre><code class="language-r">patient_source_check &lt;- registry_check_sources(
  ids = &quot;plos_one&quot;,
  timeout = 20
)

patient_source_check</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The PLOS ONE source is given up to 20 seconds to respond; an unanswered request is reported as unreachable rather than being called a broken page.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `registry_entry_template()`

Create a registry-entry template

Start a new specification with a complete YAML template instead of trying to remember the registry schema. The template separates requirements that are stated, requirements confirmed as absent and fields that have not yet been reviewed.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
# No setup is required.
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>id</code></td><td>Short identifier beginning with a lower-case letter and containing only lower-case letters, numbers and underscores.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Choose a short stable id that begins with a lower-case letter and uses only lower-case letters, numbers and underscores. Users will type this id when selecting the specification.</p><pre><code class="language-r">template_by_id &lt;- registry_entry_template(
  id = &quot;example_research_report&quot;,
  name = &quot;Example research report&quot;,
  source_url = &quot;internal:report-style-guide&quot;
)

template_by_id</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> A YAML entry beginning with example_research_report is printed and returned as text, ready to complete and validate.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>name</code></td><td>Publication, publisher, project or organisation name.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Use the full human-readable name of the publication, project or organisation. It is shown in reports, while the shorter id is used in code.</p><pre><code class="language-r">named_template &lt;- registry_entry_template(
  id = &quot;global_health_report&quot;,

  source_url = &quot;internal:global-health-style&quot;
)

named_template</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The generated entry keeps the full report name for user-facing summaries and the shorter id for function calls.</p></div></details></td></tr>
<tr><td><code>source_url</code></td><td>Page or internal record from which the requirements will be taken. HTTP(S), file: and internal: addresses are accepted.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Record the page or internal document from which the requirements will be taken. Keeping it in the template makes later checking and updating possible.</p><pre><code class="language-r">sourced_template &lt;- registry_entry_template(
  id = &quot;example_journal&quot;,
  name = &quot;Example Journal&quot;,
  source_url = &quot;https://example.org/author-guidance&quot;
)

sourced_template</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The source address is written into the template alongside today's review date so future maintainers can trace and revisit it.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>

### `registry_validate_file()`

Check a registry file before loading it

Validate a registry file before loading or contributing it. The check reads the actual YAML and reports all detected problems together, including missing provenance, invalid dates, unsupported fields and impossible numeric values.

<details class="fs-function-setup"><summary>Run the example setup</summary>
<div class="fs-argument-example-body"><pre><code class="language-r">
valid_registry_file &lt;- tempfile(fileext = &quot;.yml&quot;)
writeLines(
  c(
    &quot;journals:&quot;,
    &quot;- id: research_report&quot;,
    &quot;  name: Research report&quot;,
    &quot;  source_url: internal:report-guide&quot;,
    paste0(&quot;  verified_on: '&quot;, Sys.Date(), &quot;'&quot;),
    &quot;  requirements:&quot;,
    &quot;    columns: {compact: 85, full: 170}&quot;,
    &quot;    dpi_min: 300&quot;,
    &quot;    formats: [png]&quot;
  ),
  valid_registry_file
)

invalid_registry_file &lt;- tempfile(fileext = &quot;.yml&quot;)
writeLines(
  c(
    &quot;journals:&quot;,
    &quot;- id: Invalid ID&quot;,
    &quot;  name: Broken example&quot;,
    &quot;  verified_on: yesterday&quot;,
    &quot;  requirements:&quot;,
    &quot;    dpi_min: -10&quot;,
    &quot;    invented_field: true&quot;
  ),
  invalid_registry_file
)
</code></pre></div></details>

<table class="table fs-options-table">
<colgroup><col style="width:26%"><col style="width:74%"></colgroup>
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Option</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td><code>path</code></td><td>Path to a YAML file in registry format.<details class="fs-argument-example"><summary>See how to use it</summary><div class="fs-argument-example-body"><p>Pass one YAML file in figspec registry format. Validation does not add its entries to the current session, so you can correct problems before calling spec_load().</p><pre><code class="language-r">validation_results &lt;- c(
  valid = registry_validate_file(
    path = valid_registry_file
  ),
  invalid = registry_validate_file(
    path = invalid_registry_file
  )
)

validation_results</code></pre><p class="fs-example-result"><strong>Result:</strong> The valid file returns TRUE. The invalid file returns FALSE and reports its malformed id, missing source, invalid date, negative resolution and unsupported field together.</p></div></details></td></tr>
</tbody></table>
